brief: Goldman Sachs (David Mericle) added a 25bp hike to its September FOMC forecast after the August CPI report pushed market-implied hike odds near 90%, also raising its terminal-rate forecast to 3.25-3.5% and moving two expected 2027 cuts from June/December to September/December. GS argues there is no strong economic case for hiking: the 2% overshoot reflects fading one-time factors, core PCE has slowed to roughly 2.5% over the last three months, high inflation is not broad-based once tariff effects are excluded, inflation expectations remain anchored, and the economy is not overheated. It expects the FOMC to hike reluctantly with a minimal statement change and no forward guidance, Governor Waller to dissent because inflation is now below the 2.8% threshold he set for holding, and the FOMC to talk down (via Chair Warsh's press conference, not the statement) market pricing of an October hike, aided by investors already viewing the midterms as an obstacle. GS's dot-plot baseline is a 10-8 majority for one 2026 hike, with risk of two if participants read the hike as a normal response to oil prices and AI demand rather than reluctant acquiescence; its probability-weighted rate path stays less hawkish than market pricing.

cards.anchor: We continue to expect two cuts in 2027 but now expect them in September and December (vs. June and December previously).
